data.narrative:
Astrolight, a seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Laurynas Mačiulis, has raised €2.8M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 13 comparable companies: 5 public equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is applicable. This approach uses the €2.8M raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of €7M. The public-comp anchoring method cannot be deployed because Astrolight's revenue is not on file; while the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 27.4x revenue across six public comparables, applying this multiple requires disclosed revenue. The peer-median method similarly fails due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables with disclosed valuations in the sector.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €6M to €8M, with a median point of €7M. This range reflects the stage-progression result narrowed by a ±15% confidence band given reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include: the absence of revenue data preventing multiple triangulation; limited private-company disclosure at seed stage within aerospace; and the wide dispersion of public-sector multiples (27.4x) relative to early-stage risk. The valuation should be revisited upon disclosure of near-term revenue guidance or additional financing rounds.
